hook_text: One small house, half an hour with a notebook, seventy plastic items. Every one chosen for a reason.
clip_script: Audit a home room by room and three groups appear. Built into the walls for forty years: PVC pipes that never rust, conduit, uPVC window frames that never need paint, a polyethylene tank on the roof. Used for years: polypropylene kettle, chairs, buckets and microwave tubs; HDPE bottles and chopping boards; ABS fridge liner and TV; nylon bristles; foam mattress; melamine plates that take heat but not the microwave. Used for a day: PET bottles and LDPE bags, the biggest group and the one that ends in the river. Safety: polypropylene in the microwave, not polystyrene; keep plastic out of the sun and off the stove; small parts away from babies; plastic burns, so smoke alarm. For every item ask: right plastic, lasts long enough, and what is its next life.
visual_style: Whiteboard house cutaway with items lighting up by room; three bins labelled 40 years, 10 years, 1 day filling at different rates; a microwave with tick on polypropylene and cross on polystyrene.
mood: Home-tour curiosity with a safety edge.
pacing: Audit, built-in, durable, packaging, safety, three questions.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count the plastic items in your kitchen, then sort them into forty years, ten years and one day.
